newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher in light pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher in light pre-holiday trade.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended higher Tuesday, retaining early gains made on a strong oil futures in London amid no news and light volume ahead of the Christmas holiday Wednesday, traders said.
The session was shortened to end at 1300 EST. Traders said a couple of large firms had bought gasoline and crude which kept smaller players from selling.

"The paper (large firms) like it above $25.00, so that's why it's there," said one New York crude dealer, noting there was little else to influence prices in lacklustre trade. February crude settled up 31 cents at $25.10 a barrel.
January gasoline ended up 0.66 cent at 69.56 cents a gallon while January heating oil ended up 0.32 cent at 71.40 cents a gallon.

On the International Petroleum Exchange in London, February Brent had closed up 20 cents at $23.40 a barrel boosted by January gas oil, the European equivalent of heating oil, which ended up $4.00 at $215.50 a tonne on cold weather.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) will release its weekly oil inventory data on Thursday instead of its regularly scheduled time of Tuesday evening since the API is closed for the holiday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
